The orphan PCI4 6.3.2 (inventory of bespoke and custom software) should map to CM-8, the spine's system component inventory control. Force-fitting it onto a loosely-related control would claim coverage the control does not provide — a false equivalence that turns an honest, cheaply-fixable MODEL-stage gap into a hidden future audit finding.

save-reflection t7
The exact claim is false because PR.DS-01 (data-at-rest protection) also requires key management (SC-12) and validated cryptography (SC-13): an encrypted laptop disk whose keys are unmanaged or whose algorithm is weak does not satisfy the outcome, so SC-28 alone only overlaps it — the honest label is partial.

edit README.md
# Crosswalk README

This table maps each external framework requirement (a profile row) onto the one internal control catalog we own: the spine, NIST 800-53. 800-53 is the spine and not one of the profiles because it is the superset — the largest, most granular public catalog — so mapping a smaller framework onto it runs downhill instead of leaving requirements homeless. Read each row's relationship label as an honesty call about how much of the requirement the spine control covers: exact means they mean the same thing, broader means the spine control covers the requirement and more, narrower means it answers only part, and partial means they merely overlap. The validator guarantees structure only: every row maps to a real spine family, no orphan hides, and every label comes from the allowed vocabulary. It deliberately cannot judge whether a label is true — that semantic honesty is supplied by a human, on purpose. Treat a PASS as the floor, not the grade.

save-reflection t10
A program that builds one control set per framework ends up running five overlapping sets that are mostly the same control said five ways, each with its own evidence and owner, drifting apart until a control that satisfies one framework quietly stops satisfying another. The way out is to stop treating frameworks as the source of truth: keep ONE catalog you own — the spine — and treat each framework as a profile, a view that selects its slice of the spine through a crosswalk whose every line carries an honest relationship label. SOC 2 is an attestation report against Trust Services Criteria; ISO 27001 is a certifiable management system; CSF 2.0 is a set of outcomes organized by function; CIS v8 is a prioritized, prescriptive safeguard list. Build the control once on the spine, evidence it once, and let the crosswalk answer everyone.
